newsitem.title: GERMANY: Summer snowplows to clean up after Berlin ravers.
newsitem.headline: Summer snowplows to clean up after Berlin ravers.

text.p: Berlin, bracing for an onslaught of a million ravers for this weekend's Love Parade dance fest, said on Wednesday it would have to roll out its snowplows in the summer heat to clean up all the garbage they leave behind.

The city's sanitation department (BSR) decided not to set up extra garbage cans for the techno music fans because it found in the past few street dancers could wriggle out of the throbbing crowds to throw away their refuse properly.
Visitors to the Love Parade, a city "tradition" now in its eighth year, often turn the garbage cans into impromptu stages anyway to dance above the partying hordes.
"We decided that garbage containers make no sense at the Love Parade," BSR spokeswoman Sabine Thuemler said.
"Even people with the best intentions (of disposing of their garbage properly) literally get carried along by the masses and cannot get to the bins."
Last year, the Love Parade drew 750,000 music lovers from across the world to dance down a six km (four mile) stretch of a central Berlin boulevard closed off for the event.

Environmentalists tried to stop the event this year by raising the spectre of mountains of cans littering the avenue and human waste flooding the neighbouring Tiergarten park during the weekend the city plays host to the giant rave.

But the techno music fest has won powerful backers since its modest launch in 1989, including Mayor Eberhard Diepgen, by resuscitating the Berlin tourist industry and bringing thousands of marks to the city's empty coffers.

BSR officials and private sanitation firm Alba insist they are prepared for the refuse of the partying hordes, equipped with a fleet of 69 clean-up vehicles including garbage trucks, street cleaners and eight snowplows.

Fifty-six cabins with 12 toilets each will serve the entire parade. Thuemler said the department had decided against individual booths because of the danger that ravers would also climb atop them to dance and tip them over.
City workers have erected metal spikes on the stately gaslight posts lining the parade route to prevent visitors eager for a better view from scaling them.

The BSR and Alba promised to recycle as much of the garbage as possible. Because the bulk of the waste is comprised of aluminum cans, Thuemler said the garbage would be immediately sorted and taken to recycling centres.
Despite all the preparations, nobody knows who will pick up the estimated 270,000 mark ($150,000) bill for the clean-up.
"Since the Love Parade has grown and grown, this has been a constant source of conflict for the city," Thuemler said. "That we still don't have this resolved speaks for itself."
